event.name: LIST Golf Scotland 2026 Championship
event.tagline: 7 Days. 6 Courses. 11 Players. Organized by Chris Sewell.
event.location: St Andrews & The Kingdom of Fife, Scotland

players.name: Bart Lorang
players.bio: Spiritual founder of LIST Golf. Showed up with a passport and a grin. Chris Sewell handled every detail this year — logistics, transport, Airbnbs, the works. Bart's job is to hit fairways, buy rounds, and look distinguished.

players.name: Chris Sewell
players.bio: The man who actually made this trip happen. Chris Sewell organized every detail — Airbnbs, Platinum Cabs, tee times, the Daily Lottery entries, flight coordination, and making sure 11 dudes didn't miss their connections. Playing off a 16.1 while running the whole show. Absolute legend.

players.name: Ken Yuasa
players.bio: Lufthansa traveler arriving Saturday. Ken brings steady play and a 16.1 handicap to the team events. Riding with Bart from the airport.

players.name: Brent Nienaber
players.bio: Early bird arriving Friday via Delta. Brent's 18.3 handicap belies a competitive fire that comes out on the links. Virgin Atlantic homeward bound.

players.name: Zach Sennett
players.bio: One of the lower handicaps in the field at 12.1. Zach (ZPS) is a serious contender for the championship. Denver to EWR to EDI routing.

players.name: Jeff Karges
players.bio: The ringer. At a 7.0 handicap, Jeff is the lowest handicap in the field and the man to beat. Illinois native flying in Friday. Watch for his long drive entries.

players.name: Brad Otto
players.bio: Brad's handicap may be unlisted but his enthusiasm is not. Flying Delta to EDI Friday with Brent. Ready to battle in the team events.

players.name: Chad Kochenberger
players.bio: Chad brings a 14.6 handicap and Denver grit to the Scotland links. United Airlines through EWR. A steady presence in the team formats.

players.name: Graham Johnson
players.bio: Boston boy making the trip across the pond. Graham at 16.7 is playing The Old Course solo for bonus points. Always a threat for bonus points.

players.name: Adriaan Zimmerman
players.bio: Adriaan already played The Old Course solo on Monday (Rd 2), banking 10 bonus points. Denver-based with a 15.9 handicap. Early Friday arrival.

players.name: Ronny Hise
players.bio: The Texas cowboy of the group. Ronny's 19.1 is the highest handicap in the field but he just shot a personal best 86 at The Old Course. Never count him out.

courses.name: Eden Course at St. Andrews
courses.description: The Eden Course is the second oldest at the St Andrews Links Trust, designed by Harry Colt in 1912. A classic links layout that runs alongside the famous Eden Estuary. With generous fairways and subtle greens, it's the perfect opening round course — approachable but punishing if you lose focus. The closing stretch along the estuary is spectacular on a calm day and brutal in the wind.
courses.signature: The par-3 8th plays along the estuary edge, wind howling off the North Sea.
courses.trolleys: Available on the day at the starter (£6.50 each, cannot be pre-booked)
highlights: Eden Estuary views on back nine
Perfect warm-up for the week ahead
Wind off the North Sea tests every club

courses.name: The Castle Course at St. Andrews
courses.description: The newest of the St Andrews Links courses (opened 2008), the Castle Course sits dramatically on a cliff-top overlooking St Andrews Bay. David McLay Kidd's design is a modern links with jaw-dropping views of the town, the Old Course, and the North Sea. The greens are famously undulating — some of the most challenging in Scotland. Not your grandfather's links; this is a 21st-century test.
courses.signature: The par-4 15th plays from the highest point on the course with a 360-degree view of Fife.
courses.trolleys: Available on the day at the starter (£6.50 each, cannot be pre-booked)
highlights: Some of Scotland's most challenging greens

courses.name: Lundin Links
courses.description: A true hidden gem of Scottish golf. Lundin Links is a classic James Braid-designed links that has hosted Open Qualifying. The course runs along the Fife coast with heather-lined fairways, deep pot bunkers, and some of the most authentic links terrain you'll find outside the big names. The opening holes are a gentle handshake; the middle stretch is a fistfight with the elements.
courses.signature: The par-4 14th 'The Gotten' — a blind tee shot over a ridge to a punchbowl fairway, with the sea beyond.

courses.name: Crail Balcomie
courses.description: Crail Golfing Society is the 7th oldest golf club in the world (founded 1786). The Balcomie Links is a Tom Morris design that hugs the Fife coast tighter than any course you'll play. At just over 6,000 yards it's short by modern standards, but the narrow fairways, gorse bushes, and coastal winds make it play every inch of its length. This is old-school golf — no frills, just pure links.
courses.signature: The par-4 2nd plays along the clifftop with the North Sea roaring below — one of the most photographed holes in Fife.
courses.trolleys: TBD if extra fee (included in reservation)
highlights: Founded 1786 — 7th oldest golf club in the world

courses.name: Aberdour Golf Club
courses.description: A shorter but no-less-charming parkland/links hybrid on the Firth of Forth. Aberdour offers a different test — tree-lined in places, coastal in others, with views across the water to Edinburgh. The shorter length (par 64) means birdie opportunities are there for the taking, but accuracy is at a premium. A beautiful palate cleanser after four days of pure links golf.
courses.signature: The par-3 6th plays downhill to a green framed by the Firth of Forth — a wedge and a prayer.
courses.trolleys: TBD if extra fee (included in reservation)
highlights: Scenic contrast to the pure links courses

courses.name: Dumbarnie Links
courses.description: The grand finale. Dumbarnie Links opened in 2020 to instant acclaim — a modern links that feels like it's been here for centuries. Designed by Clive Clark, it's built on stunning duneland along the Fife coast. Every hole has sea views. The routing is a masterpiece: the front nine tumbles through dunes, the back nine opens up to sweeping vistas. A fitting final battleground for the championship.
courses.signature: The par-4 13th plays from a dune-top tee to a fairway that falls away to the sea — pure drama.

formatRules.description: Each player plays their own ball; the team's lowest score on each hole counts.
Each player plays their own ball; the individual's lowest score wins the skin.
Groups determined day-of by group consensus.
Team selects the best shot after every stroke; both players hit from that spot until holed.
Team selects the best drive; each player then plays their own ball until holed.
Each player plays their own ball; both scores are combined.

scoringRules.rule: Each player receives 1 Press per 9 holes. Call 'Press' while the tee shot is in the air to add 1 skin to that hole.
Unused Presses automatically apply to the final hole (at 9 & 18).
Birdie = 2x skins on the line for that hole.
Eagle = 5x skins on the line for that hole.
Hole-in-One = 100x skins on the line for that hole.
If the match is tied on 18, skins on the line are rounded up and divided evenly.

bonusRules.name: Long Drive
bonusRules.description: Each 9 includes 1 Long Drive (ball must finish in the fairway) — Longest Par 5 on that nine

bonusRules.name: Japan
bonusRules.description: Each 9 includes 1 Closest to Pin 'Japan' (ball must finish on the green) — Shortest Par 3 on that nine

oldCourseSolo.description: Players can book a solo round at The Old Course (via the Daily Lottery ballot). Each successful solo round earns 10 bonus points to the championship total.
